title: A Manual of Penetrating Thrusts Through Plate and Hide
summary: Teaches full-meridian spear users how to drive a thrust through plate, thick hide and layered padding.

title: Spear Against Many: A Treatise on Crowded Fighting
summary: A treatise on a lone spear user holding several opponents at bay with sweeps, points and constant movement.

title: The Return of the Haft: Advanced Whirling Forms
summary: A manual of advanced whirls of the shaft in which every strike travels out and returns in one continuous turn.

title: Field Canon of the Qi-Filled Spear
summary: A canon for users whose qi has become a field, teaching them to fill the whole spear and the ground before it.

title: Reach Beyond the Point: A Treatise on Qi Extension
summary: Teaches users of the qi field to extend the point's strike beyond the metal without any loss of control.

title: The Paired Reed Spear Course
summary: A course in which the spear is carried in two linked tracks of motion, one of the hands and one of the feet.

title: Hawk-Stoop Spear Treatise
summary: A treatise on the downward strike like a hawk's stoop, with climbing steps and sudden descent of the point.

title: River-Bend Spear Forms of the Dual Track
summary: Sets out forms in which thrusts curve like a river bend, with one track of the qi going straight and one turning.

title: Twin-Court Spear Canon of Two Currents
summary: Holds two currents of qi, one hard and one yielding, in the same spear and teaches the move between them.

title: The Wind-Sworn Spearman's Bearing
summary: Sets out the stance and bearing of the wind-sworn spearman who holds a line in the open with no cover.

title: Plateau Edge Spear Oaths and Thrusts
summary: Pairs each thrust with a short oath of purpose, teaching that a sworn line is held to the end.

title: Gale-Line Spear Book of Open Ground
summary: A book for the qi-field spear user on open ground, in which the field is set like a gale along the point.

title: Oath-Bound Haft: Bearing and Thrust on the High Plain
summary: Binds the qi field to a sworn bearing so that the haft never loses line however fierce the plateau wind.
